title: The Wise Men of Chelm and the Knocking Shutters
summary: Yokel the shammes is old, and he is tired of knocking on every single shutter at night to wake Chelm for prayers. The Wise Men of Chelm come up with a brilliant plan: bring all the shutters to the courtyard and knock on them all at once! What a boom, what a commotion... and who stays asleep in the end? A rhyming story based on a folk tale of the Wise Men of Chelm.
pages:
Old Yokel the shammes, each night he would rise
before all of Chelm, under pitch-black skies.
"Knock-knock-knock! Wake up, Chelmites, rise!
The stars are all closing their sleepy eyes!"

A hundred houses in Chelm, each with a shutter on the wall,
and Yokel knocks, and knocks, and knocks... no miracle at all!
"Knock-knock-knock! Wake up, Chelmites, rise!
The stars are all closing their sleepy eyes!"

But Yokel grew weary, his legs ached and were sore.
He sat on a step and he sighed, "Oh, these nights are such a chore!
A hundred shutters in Chelm, and only two legs for me!
One more night like this, and twice as old I'll be!"

The three wise men thought, and they scratched at their beards,
till Reb Shmerel raised a finger: "I've a little idea, my dears!
Why should Yokel run to each shutter, one by one?
Let the shutters come to him! That's the miracle, and done!"

The four strongest men took the shutters down from every window frame,
and stood them in the courtyard in rows and rows and rows, all the same.

Yokel lifted a hammer, so heavy and so grand,
and banged on all the shutters at once: BOOM! Like thunder, like a drum, like a pot slipping out of a hand!
"Boom-boom-boom! Wake up, Chelmites, rise!
The stars are all closing their sleepy eyes!"

All of Chelm jumped out of bed, nightcaps swinging to and fro,
and ran to the courtyard, eyes shut and mouths half open, still asleep and dreaming as they go.

Everyone searched for his own shutter, but the shutters looked like twins!
"That's mine!" "No, mine!" "Maybe it's..." No names, no marks, so where does one begin?

When the sun came up, each one carried a shutter home, almost his own,
and in the synagogue they prayed with joy, in a loud and clear tone.

But who was left in the courtyard, on the very last pile of shutters, deep?
Yokel the shammes! Hugging his hammer, hat over his eyes, like a baby fast asleep.

"Shhh..." whispered Gittele, "let him sleep some more!"
All of Chelm tiptoed by without a sound; even the rooster understood, and didn't crow one cock-a-doodle more.

But at last, when the sun was shining high in the sky,
Gittele took a teeny hammer and, with both hands, knocked gently and slowly, close by:
"Knock-knock-knock! Wake up, Chelmites, rise!
The stars are all closing their sleepy eyes!"
